journey.note: Tribunal (Shahdara, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi) awarded Rs 2,92,464 with 12% interest: income at unskilled minimum wage Rs 8,086, functional disability 7%, no future prospects.
Claimant's appeal allowed: functional disability raised to 13%, future prospects of 40% added, pain and suffering raised to Rs 75,000; award enhanced by Rs 2,08,871 with 12% interest.

extraction.title_anon: Man, 34, security guard, Delhi (injury, leg fractures)
extraction.family_summary: A 34-year-old security guard and his wife were travelling on a cycle rickshaw in March 2014 when a car hit it, and he suffered fractures of his left thigh bone and shin. In November 2016 a tribunal in Delhi awarded him Rs 2,92,464 with 12% interest. He appealed, and in September 2026 the Delhi High Court raised the award to Rs 5,01,335. The case took about twelve and a half years from the accident, about nine of them in the High Court.
what_mattered: The High Court used the full 13% disability on his certificate, not 7%, to work out his lost earnings. It accepted his lawyer's argument that he would not get a security guard's job again, saying the kind of work a person does is critical in judging how much a disability affects earning.
Because he was 34, the High Court added 40% to his monthly income (Rs 3,234 on top of Rs 8,086) to allow for the pay rises he would likely have had; the tribunal had added nothing.
He had no proof of his Rs 15,000 salary, so income stayed at the unskilled minimum wage of Rs 8,086 a month; pain and suffering rose from Rs 40,000 to Rs 75,000 under a 2024 Supreme Court ruling.
